harmonicFunction: D (I) - Tonic major chord delivering bright, optimistic 1950s rockabilly drive
Dsus4 (Isus4) - Suspended embellishment created by hammering the pinky on the 3rd fret high E string
G (IV) - Subdominant chord adding buoyant bounce on the backbeat
C (bVII) - Flattened seventh providing classic rockabilly swagger and blues color
Bb (bVI) - Chromatic modal interchange borrowed from minor, building dramatic tension before the turnaround
E7 (V/V) - Secondary dominant leading with harmonic urgency into the dominant A chord

techniques.name: Rockabilly Acoustic Dsus4 Shuffle
techniques.description: Freddie Mercury's percussive acoustic rhythm style. Holding a standard open D major chord while rhythmically hammering and pulling off the pinky finger on the 3rd fret high E string to alternate between D and Dsus4 on the upbeats

notes: Form open D chord with index (fret 2, string 3), ring (fret 3, string 2), and middle (fret 2, string 1)
Hammer down the pinky firmly onto the 3rd fret high E string to sound Dsus4
Pull off cleanly back to the 2nd fret (F#) to resolve to D major
Maintain a crisp swing shuffle feel (long-short eighth-note subdivisions)
Keep strings 6 and 5 muted with the thumb hooked over the neck
sequence: Downstroke the open D chord on beat 1
Hammer on the pinky on the upbeat of beat 1 to sound Dsus4
Pull off to D on beat 2 with a percussive pick-hand brush
Repeat the syncopated hammer-pull cycle in steady shuffle tempo at 154 BPM
tips: Use a thin or medium nylon plectrum to get a bright, snappy acoustic strumming sound
Keep your wrist loose and bouncy; the groove comes from wrist swing, not stiff forearm movement
Let the open 4th string (D) ring loud and proud as the foundational bass note
details.progression: D - Dsus4 - D - G - C - G

techniques.name: Vintage Telecaster Double-Stop Bends
techniques.description: Brian May's departure from his usual Red Special guitar. Playing a 1967 Fender Telecaster through a cranked tube amp to deliver authentic 1950s rockabilly twang, featuring oblique double-stop bends and country-style snap

notes: Switch to the bridge pickup of a single-coil guitar for piercing vintage bite
Hold down the note on string 2 while bending the note on string 3 a full step upward
Apply snappy hybrid picking (pick on lower string, middle finger popping the higher string)
Incorporate a tight 120 ms slapback tape echo with a single repeat
sequence: Fret string 2 at fret 10 with index finger
Bend string 3 at fret 12 up a full step to pitch with ring and middle fingers
Strike both strings together for a crying country-rockabilly unison dissonance
Release into rapid descending pentatonic pull-offs
tips: Keep your bend strictly in tune; an under-bent double stop sounds sour
Roll off amp bass frequencies slightly to prevent low-end flub on fast runs
Add subtle fret-hand slap on the guitar body during the drum breaks

sections.name: Acoustic Strum & Dsus4 Snapping Intro
sections.description: Freddie Mercury's solo acoustic guitar establishes the relentless rockabilly swing shuffle, snapping between D and Dsus4 before hitting the punchy G-C-G cadence.
sections.progression: D - Dsus4 - D - G - C - G
notes: Lock into the 154 BPM swing eighth-note shuffle feel
Snap pinky hammer-ons on the high E string with crisp definition
Hit the C major chord with authoritative downbeat punch
Mute strings 6 and 5 cleanly throughout

sections.name: Verse Rockabilly Shuffle & Walking Bass
sections.description: John Deacon's upright-style walking bass enters alongside Roger Taylor's crisp snare brushes. Freddie's acoustic comping drives the storytelling vocal delivery.
sections.progression: D - G - C - G - D - Bb - C - D
notes: Keep the strumming hand bouncy and light to complement the walking bass
Accent the backbeat snare cracks on beats 2 and 4
Execute the clean chromatic shift from Bb to C with quick barre shifts
Resolve cleanly to the open D chord ringout

sections.name: Chorus Handclap Stomp & Turnaround
sections.description: The band locks into infectious handclaps and stomps. The harmony maneuvers through G, C, and Bb before resolving through E7 to the dominant A turnaround.
sections.progression: G - C - G - Bb - E7 - A
notes: Strum with open, celebratory energy matching the handclaps
Accentuate the secondary dominant E7 chord to build harmonic tension
Deliver the four descending eighth-note walking notes into A
Leave a dramatic pause right before Freddie's vocal re-entry

sections.name: Brian May Rockabilly Twang Solo
sections.description: Brian May delivers a legendary, authentic rockabilly lead guitar clinic on a vintage Telecaster, executing double-stop bends, blues curls, and rapid country-style pull-offs.
sections.progression: D - G - D - G - Bb - C - D
notes: Bend the G string at fret 12 while holding the B string at fret 10 steady
Dig into the pick attack for the biting bridge single-coil twang
Let the slapback echo bounce once per phrase
Execute rapid descending blues pull-offs cleanly without fret buzzing

sections.name: A Cappella Breakdown & Finger Snaps
sections.description: Instruments cut out completely for Queen's breathtaking multi-tracked vocal harmonies, finger snaps, and foot stomps, highlighting the pristine songwriting craft.
notes: Mute strings entirely; do not allow incidental string noise
Count the swing pulse internally to prepare for the explosive band re-entry
Listen to Freddie's vocal pitch cues for the incoming D chord attack
sections.exerciseLabel: A Cappella Break & Silent Pulse Count

sections.name: Outro Rhythm Drive & Walking Turnaround
sections.description: The full band charges back in for the grand finale. Acoustic shuffle strumming and twangy Telecaster fills interweave until the triumphant final guitar chord ringout.
notes: Strum with maximum joyous swing energy
Add subtle high-register fills between acoustic strums
Follow the tempo slightly accelerating into the final hit
Conclude with a sharp, crisp D major staccato chord choke

commonMistakes: Playing straight eighth notes instead of the essential swing/shuffle feel
Letting the pinky drag or mute the adjacent B string during Dsus4 hammer-ons
Under-bending the double stop in the solo, resulting in sour, jarring dissonance
Strumming strings 6 and 5 during the open D chord, muddying the acoustic clarity
